Tenable One AI Exposure FAQs What is AI security? AI security (also known as AI cybersecurity ) encompasses two categories: AI for security and security for AI . AI for security applies artificial intelligence to strengthen your organization’s cyber defenses. It speaks to security technology vendors who build AI into their products and to security teams leveraging AI to improve productivity and efficiency. The Tenable Vulnerability Priority Rating (VPR) is an example of AI for security. VPR leverages machine learning and RAG-based large language models (LLM) to forecast the likelihood an attacker will exploit any given vulnerability to inform prioritization. Tenable One harnesses generative AI, deep learning, and machine learning to unify your security lifecycle by enabling natural language investigations, accelerating asset discovery, and transforming complex findings into precise step-by-step mitigation plans for your entire exposure surface. Meanwhile, security for AI mitigates the security risks stemming from consuming or building AI. Tenable One for AI Exposure is an example of security for AI. What is Tenable One AI Exposure? Tenable One AI Exposure helps your organization secure and understand how you’re using AI. It delivers visibility, context, and control to manage AI risk from enterprise AI platforms, so you can govern AI use, enforce policies, and prevent exposures. What are Tenable One Identity Exposure’s main capabilities? Tenable One Identity Exposure, an identity security solution, helps you unify human and machine identities into a single consolidated view, map risky relationships to visualize how attackers move laterally, and secure your infrastructure by detecting and neutralizing threats like Kerberoasting and DCSync in real time. Is Tenable One a point-in-time security audit tool for hybrid environments? Web application scanning is a critical part of the Tenable One exposure management platform . Tenable One Web App Scanning is a dynamic application security testing (DAST) application. A DAST crawls a running web application through the front end to create a site map with all of the pages, links, and forms for testing. Once the DAST creates a site map, it interrogates the site through the front end to identify any vulnerabilities in the application’s custom code or known vulnerabilities in the third-party components that comprise the bulk of the application. What kind of vulnerabilities does Tenable One Web App Scanning identify? Tenable One Web App Scanning identifies OWASP Top 10 web application vulnerabilities , such as cross-site scripting (XSS) and SQL injection in custom application code and vulnerable versions of third-party components running on your site. Does Tenable One Web App Scanning identify misconfigurations or certificate issues? Yes. You can use Tenable One Web App Scanning to identify a number of cyber hygiene issues in web applications in two minutes or less using predefined scan templates. The SSL/TLS scan template checks for improperly issued or soon-to-expire SSL/TLS certificates, which helps users avoid costly and embarrassing browser warnings and redirects. The Config Audit scan template checks for a number of server-side misconfigurations that leave web applications vulnerable to hacker reconnaissance or man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks.
